free_tier.stated: no service and no account; source under MIT

egress.terms: not applicable; the software states no volume; ingress: tcp

interface_detail: wg-tcp-tunnel --src-tcp/--dst-udp on one end, --src-udp/--dst-tcp on the other
tooling: cmake plus Boost.Asio; systemd and Termux runit units in tree
chaining: composes with any TCP forwarder that hands over a raw stream, including an ngrok TCP endpoint, and with a plain public-IP host.
binding_note: the constraint is a public-IP server at the far end, outside the vocabulary; the build can also reach the far end through ngrok

identity_cost.detail: no account; a public-IP server and a client

reliability_note: source-built only; no release artefacts; the ngrok path inherits ngrok's connection accounting
confidence_note: a measured run through the ngrok path would raise it, and would be the first measurement of a hosted tunnel carrying WireGuard

evidence.proved: the purpose sentence, both invocations, and the Endpoint rewrite
"-DENABLE_NGROK=ON ... --ngrok-api-key=KEY --ngrok-dst-tcp-endpoint=ENDPOINT"; the tunnel can use an NGROK endpoint as its destination
tags v1.1.2 latest, no GitHub release objects, last commit 2026-08-28; 38 stars

notes: The only wrapper that ships a mode for a hosted forwarder by name: with -DENABLE_NGROK=ON the client dials an ngrok TCP endpoint instead of the server's IP. That is the shortest documented path from a free hosted tunnel to a WireGuard datagram, and it costs one ngrok connection from the free monthly allowance. No release object exists, so a deployment builds from source with Boost and CMake.

extras.wg_detail: "This project is a simple UDP-over-TCP tunneling. The main purpose of it is to allow WireGuard to work over TCP"; server '--src-tcp=0.0.0.0:51820 --dst-udp=127.0.0.1:51820', client '--src-udp=127.0.0.1:51822 --dst-tcp=<SERVER-IP>:51820' with Endpoint = 127.0.0.1:51822
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the software states no volume
extras.transit_note: the far end forwards into the local WireGuard listener
extras.hosting_requirement: a host on a public address running the server half, or an ngrok TCP endpoint in its place
